short_answer: Steve Fezzik is a real, well known Las Vegas bettor. The Las Vegas Sun reported in January 2010 that he won the Las Vegas Hilton Supercontest two years in a row, and official 2025 standings we opened show an entry under the alias FEZZIK-1 winning the Westgate SuperContest second half contest and an entry FEZZIK-3 tied for 9th in the Circa Sports Million. In that sense he is legitimate.

Contest results are not the same product as the picks he sells. Contest players pick five NFL games a week against fixed contest lines, and he often plays several entries. His paid picks at SIC Picks sit behind a login, and the unit totals in his marketing (+215, +241, +257 and +500 units over various spans) come from him or his sellers, not from a full public log we could open.

Treat Fezzik as a proven contest player whose paid record is unproven for today's buyer. If you buy, buy a week first, log every pick with the line and time you received it, and judge it over a full season or more.

guarantee: We found no guarantee on any Steve Fezzik package. Each package lists what is included: futures, sides, totals, props, and email and SMS pick alerts. The SIC FAQ says: "Purchases are non-refundable unless a specific promotion, guarantee, or written policy states otherwise."

The packages are shown as priced "/ yearly" or "/ weekly". The SIC terms say paid services are "typically offered in annual increments or by a specific sporting period season" and allow automatic card payments if you choose them. We did not find clear wording on whether a weekly package renews on its own, so check your account settings after you buy. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: The unit totals do not agree with each other. For 2020 to 2024 his Pregame bio says +241 units, his own website says +257, and in a January 2026 forum reply he wrote that he won "just under 260 UNITS". The SIC page uses a different span, 2020 to 2026, and says +215, which implies losing results after 2024 that the older pages do not show. None of these totals comes with a public log, a unit size or the prices taken.

His contest marketing names his best entries. The Circa Sports standings list five FEZZIK entries in the 2025 Million: one tied for 9th at 56-31-3, and the others tied for 308th, 379th, 1,035th and 3,310th. The Westgate second half standings list FEZZIK-1 first at 34-10-1 and FEZZIK-2 tied for 79th at 26-18-1. For the first half, which his Pregame bio gives as 17-28, the Westgate standings show FEZZIK-1 at 18-27 and FEZZIK-2 at 20-25. Playing several entries is normal in these contests, but quoting only the best one makes the picks look better than they were on average.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: contest results published by the organizers. We opened the Westgate 2025 SuperContest standings, which show FEZZIK-1 first in the Weeks 10 to 18 contest at 34-10-1 with a $50,000 prize, and the Circa Sports Million VII full season standings, which show FEZZIK-3 tied for 9th at 56-31-3 with a $70,000 prize. The standings list aliases, not legal names, but the aliases and results match what Fezzik advertises. The Las Vegas Sun reported on 16 Jan 2010 that he won the 2009 Hilton Supercontest at 52-29-3 for $196,800, after cashing for $210,000 the year before, and called it the first back to back title in the contest's 20 year history. We did not open organizer standings for 2008 or 2009.

Those contests are a different product from the paid picks. Contest entries are five NFL sides a week against fixed lines; the packages at SIC Picks include futures, totals and props at market prices. A strong contest finish does not tell you how the paid picks did.

What the seller side publishes: the SIC FAQ says results are on the website, but the picks dashboard asked us to sign in, and we found no public log of Fezzik's SIC picks. Pregame.com still shows an archive of his Pregame picks with date, time, pick, size and result, the latest dated 5 Apr 2026. That archive was graded by the company that sold his picks, and we did not total it. In 2015 Pregame announced that a tracker called ComptrBob would log his Bet Like a Pro program in a forum thread; we opened only the first page of that 478 page thread and saw no current totals, so we make no claim about them.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Steve Fezzik pick record is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his paid picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Fezzik told the Las Vegas Sun in 2010 that hitting 57% over a contest season is improbable. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Steve Fezzik is thin and mostly comes from the Pregame.com forums, where he sold picks until April 2026. We found no reviews of his new SIC Picks packages. Below is what we read and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: A Pregame forum member posted that Fezzik "lost -95 Units for his clients in 2025" and gave no log. Fezzik replied that he won just under 260 units from 2020 to 2024 and told readers to buy another handicapper rather than him. Another member argued the totals ignored fees and lines buyers could not get. We did not verify any of these figures.
In the same thread several members defended him. One wrote that unhappy buyers at least know he has a winning track record and that he cares, judging by his reply.

A member alleged that Fezzik sent paying clients the Rams +3 while saying on a podcast that the Rams had no chance against the 49ers, and cited a 2024 paid NFL record of 62-58-2 without a source. We could not check either claim.

Fezzik posted that he would stop providing services to Pregame after the NCAA basketball games, ending about 13 years there. A video posted by Sports Injury Central about two months before our check announced that he was joining SICPicks.com.
We found no Reddit thread with a substantial discussion of his paid picks, Trustpilot did not load for our check, and we found no app store listing or customer reviews for his SIC Picks packages.

conflicts: The Sports Injury Central promotions page sends readers to prediction market apps (Kalshi, Polymarket, ProphetX and Novig) through tracked links with the promo code SIC, and offers a free week of its own picks product for signing up. That suggests SIC earns from referrals. It says nothing about Fezzik's picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.

His own website, stevefezzik.com, still says his picks are only available at Pregame.com, while the SIC page says his picks are only available at SIC. The website appears out of date; buy only through a page you can trace to him.
strengths: A real, named bettor with contest wins that the contest organizers themselves publish, and a 2010 newspaper account of his back to back title.
Prices and package contents are listed openly, with weekly options so a buyer can test before committing to a season.
He shares free material in public, such as NFL power ratings on the Pregame forums and a free weekly NFL pick at SIC.
concerns: No full public log of his SIC picks. The unit totals in his marketing come from him and his sellers.
Unit totals for the same years differ from page to page.
Contest claims quote his best entry and leave out his other entries, several of which finished far down the standings.
SIC says purchases are non refundable, and no guarantee is offered on his packages.
Discount codes and countdown banners push buyers to decide quickly.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Yes, he is a real Las Vegas bettor with contest wins reported by the Las Vegas Sun and shown on Westgate and Circa Sports standings. That proves contest success, not that his paid picks make money for buyers.
How much does Steve Fezzik cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 SIC Picks sold his NFL picks or his college football picks for $79 a week or $799 a season each, and both together for $129 a week or $1,199 a season. Discount codes were advertised, and SIC says purchases are non refundable.
Does Steve Fezzik have a verified record?

His contest results are published by the organizers, including a 2025 Westgate second half win and a tie for 9th in the 2025 Circa Million. His paid pick record is not: the unit totals come from him and his sellers, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to him.

For the money you get every NFL or college football play, or both, from a proven contest player, including futures and props, with email and SMS alerts. What is unproven is whether those paid picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over a large sample, and there is no refund if they do not.
